dedupe_keys.name: the spectrum dividend spectrum management issues oecd digital economy papers no 125 2007

description: This OECD paper, by Jaebum Lee of the Directorate for Science, Technology and Industry, discusses spectrum management issues raised by the digitalisation of terrestrial television. After analogue switch-off, a large amount of spectrum is expected to be freed for other uses, which the paper calls the spectrum dividend. Sections cover how the size of the dividend is calculated, unused channels in the terrestrial TV spectrum, possible current and future demands, the strengths and weaknesses of spectrum management approaches (one size does not fit all), and how to relocate incumbent analogue broadcasters, with an appendix of country information. The executive summary begins with a note on spectrum scarcity in about 120 countries in Europe, Africa and the Middle East. Producer: OECD, published 22 January 2007, replacing a November 2006 version. Coverage: OECD countries with a regional view of Europe, Africa and the Middle East. Access: free PDF on the OECD site; the foreword, contents and start of the summary were read. Licence and cost: free; no licence statement read. Caveats: figures date from 2006 and predate later band reallocations. Simulation uses: the dividend size calculation and the country appendix inform capacity scenarios for broadcast spectrum. Related record: the ITU digital dividend report of 2018 (data-itu-digital-dividend-insights-spectrum-decisions-2018).
